items_missed: No real agenda opener — 'I guess I'll run through a short list of questions here' sketches a roadmap but carries no time estimate and no confirmation ask, so the flag does not hit. On a call where the customer said she was in a hospital, the 10-15 minute framing mattered more than usual, not less.
Never checked Einstein's own availability for the September 16 move date — only confirmed the date on the form was correct.

Probe gaps on a 3600 sqft two-story intake: no garage, storage unit, attic, or balcony question; no long walk, narrow hallway, or tight turn question; no parking or HOA/gate access question; no additional stops; no storage stops; no stairs question for the destination home.
Never asked what she was worried about with the move — he acknowledged her situation kindly but never asked the moving-stressor question.
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned. This is not walkthrough-dependent and is the single strongest reassurance available to keep a lead warm across a five-day gap.
'No deposit required' never mentioned — a free differentiator on a call with no pricing in it.
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' — he closed on his own summary instead of opening the floor.
No business hours given; the callback path was 'call this number back or just respond to the email,' with no hours attached.
Garbled his own name four different ways across the call (Jesper, Jess, Jessica, Jessa). The customer had to interrupt to ask 'what's your name? I'm sorry' and still signed off calling him 'Justin.'
Heavy verbal filler throughout — stacked 'absolutely, absolutely,' 'okay, okay, okay, gotcha,' and several stalled restarts.

Missed the Save Your Ass reinforcement when the customer handed it to him: she said she has an SUV and 'a lot of the smaller boxes I can take over.' Not scored against him on a scheduler call, but that was the moment to confirm that every carload is time off her clock.

SCORING NOTE: this is a walkthrough_scheduler. Clock (4), Estimate (13), and Save Your Ass (10) were granted in full under the N/A rule because the call type genuinely excludes them, and the pricing mechanics inside Section 3 were granted for the same reason. 27 of the 64 points are auto-granted — do not read this score as comparable to a full sales call without that caveat.
top_strength: Excellent adaptive control of a call that could easily have died. The customer opened by saying she was in the hospital with her father and could not inventory her home, and instead of pushing or abandoning, he re-scoped in real time: 'we can chat about it a bit and then we can circle back later on because it sounds like you're a bit busy. Hope everything is okay on your end.' He then ran the form recap tightly and accurately — quote date, 9001 Thick Woods Cove, two-story, roughly 3600 sqft, downsizing to 20208 Fox Drive — and got a clean confirmation on every item. He also handled the mount policy proactively and precisely before it could become a day-of surprise, explaining that crews can take the mirror and both TVs off the wall but cannot install a mount, which the customer immediately accepted and solved herself with a handyman. Best of all, he left the call with a booked walkthrough for Thursday plus a text confirmation and a video link promised.
coaching_note: Jespah, this was a well-adapted call and you got the one thing that mattered — the walkthrough is on the calendar for Thursday with a text reminder and a link. Two fixes. First and highest leverage: you have a five-day gap before that walkthrough, and you put nothing in it to hold her. Deferring price to the email is correct on a scheduler, but No Worries coverage, Meet Your Mover, and no-deposit cost you nothing to say and are what make a customer stop shopping. Add one line before the handoff: 'Before I let you go, two things worth knowing — every move is covered up to $2,000 for accidental damage under our No Worries coverage, and there's no deposit, we only take payment when the job is done. Any other questions before I let you go?' Second: fix your own name. You gave it as Jesper, Jess, Jessica, and Jessa on one call, the customer had to ask, and she still said 'thanks, Justin' at goodbye. Pick one and open with it the same way every time. Also tighten the probe — you asked packing and boxes well, but never asked about the garage, storage, parking, or stairs at the new house, and on a 3600 sqft two-story those are exactly the variables that blow up an estimate. Note on the score: pricing, clock, estimate, and Save Your Ass were treated as out of scope for a walkthrough scheduler, so 27 points here were granted automatically. The 64 is not directly comparable to a full sales call.
phone_presence_notes: Real warmth and situational awareness — he caught the hospital comment and responded to it ('hope everything is okay on your end'), normalized her not knowing her box count ('that's totally fair, I totally get it'), and closed with 'this is a really good start, Rebecca,' and she stayed positive throughout ('that's perfect,' 'appreciate it'); held back from a 5 by the name confusion and the volume of filler.
audio_review_reason: The rep's name appears four different ways in the transcript (Jesper/Jess/Jessica/Jessa) and the customer signs off with 'Justin' — need audio to confirm whether this is a genuine clarity problem in his self-introduction or a speech-to-text artifact, since it is the main driver of the Section 9 clarity deduction.
